View on mid/small caps in tech subindustries
SPE-related
- For component-related names benefiting from WFE growth, growth rates are widening as inventory adjustments end and demand for advance orders emerges.

- In test-related areas such as testers, probers, and probe cards, demand is being created by both higher volumes of AI-related devices and the increase in test items associated with performance improvements.
- Demand for probe cards for memory is increasing not only for HBM and general purpose DRAM, but also for NAND.
- For probers, improving high precision temperature control functions and increasing supply capacity create opportunities to win orders.
- Semiconductor capex in China remains strong, and the degree of penetration into the China supply chain is becoming a differentiator in terms of earnings contributions.
Renewed focus on strength in data center-related demand
Semi materials-related
- Procurement risk related to the Middle East has eased, but high prices and delays in price pass-throughs remain risks.

- Low CTE and low dielectric materials driven by AI-related demand. Compared with quartz glass, glass cloth has inferior performance, but when combined with resin it can differentiate through CCL performance and lower processing difficulty. Low CTE glass has a technological barrier in terms of the difficulty of yarn production.

- Capacity expansion by materials companies is aimed in part at meeting demand around 2030. From land acquisition to plant construction and equipment installation, it takes at least two years to begin mass production.
- Demand for front-end materials such as photoresists, CMP slurry, and wiring related materials remains firm.
- In advanced packaging, increasing size, multilayering, and higher density are growth drivers, beyond mere volume expansion
Device-related
- Power equipment related: Demand for battery storage systems continues, and interest in transformers for private sector demand is increasing further.
- Computers: Demand related to data centers remains strong, mainly AI related. We will monitor tech developments such as vertical power delivery.
- Smartphones & PCs: We're cautious over potential demand weakness and lower production volumes triggered by rising memory prices.
- Home appliances & consumer electronics: Demand stagnation is built into company plans, reflecting factors such as inflation.
- Industrial equipment & automotive: Semiconductor- and defense-related areas are promising. In automotive, watch demand changes stemming from differences in customer mix.

Summary of this month and topics of interest (equipment-related)

Micronics Japan: (1) F12/26 1Q results had revenue at ¥20.9bn and OP at ¥5.65bn (margin 27.0%) → 2Q plan of ¥24.8bn and OP ¥7.25bn (29.3%), 3Q plan of ¥25.9bn and OP ¥9.0bn (34.7%): Margins are likely to improve toward 3Q driven by product mix improvement. (2) F12/26 revenue plan calls for growth significantly higher than +26%: MCJ added “significantly” to its previous guidance of “revenue growth above 26%”. (3) Pace of capacity expansion: MCJ looks to increase at roughly ¥2.0bn per quarter in 2026.

Tokyo Seimitsu: (1) F3/26 results had revenue at ¥166.9bn (+5% YoY; guidance ¥165.0bn) and OP at ¥33.7bn (+16%; ¥32.0bn). 4Q OP margin was 23.8% (semiconductors 26.1%), up 1.4ppt (2.0ppt) YoY, driven by a higher mix of high value-added products. (2) F3/27 guidance has revenue at ¥181.5bn (F3/28 plan is at ¥185.0bn) and OP ¥40.0bn (¥45.0bn), with margins of 22.0% (24.3%), indicating progress toward medium-term targets. (3) Semiconductor equipment 1H order plan is +20% YoY, exceeding revenue growth assumptions (1H +16%, 2H +6%).

TOWA: (1) F3/26 results showed revenue at ¥54.4bn (+2% YoY; guidance ¥54.5bn) and OP ¥6.92bn (-22%; ¥7.0bn), the latter slightly missing the downward revised plan. (2) F3/27 guidance has revenue at ¥64.0bn (1H ¥32.0bn) and OP ¥10.24bn (¥5.12bn), with quarterly order (revenue) assumptions of ¥15.0-17.0bn (¥16.0bn): While demand remains strong for HBM, general memory, and advanced packaging, uncertainty leads to a flat 1H-2H profile. (3) Looking YoY, TOWA assumes revenue growth of ¥10.5bn and OP growth of ¥1.36bn: While higher revenue is expected to contribute, initial costs for WLP equipment will weigh on margins.

Ferrotec: (1) F3/26 results put revenue at ¥288.9bn (+5% YoY; guidance ¥285.0bn) and OP at ¥27.6bn (+14%; ¥30.0bn). 4Q showed revenue of ¥77.3bn (3Q ¥70.7bn) and OP ¥5.72bn (¥7.51bn): Initial mass production costs at the Malaysia plant and valuation losses on solar quartz crucibles led to a miss vs plan. (2) Fiscal year change from F3/27 to F12/26: The company's subsidiaries close books in December, and so the revenue headwind will come from the parent's Jan-Mar sales (~¥5.0bn). (3) Semiconductor-related equipment: Ferrotec assumes +20% growth in the WFE market, with vacuum seals and metal processing (for new equipment assembly) at +38% revenue growth. (4) Thermo modules: Demand led by optical transceivers is likely to drive revenue from ¥30.8bn in F3/26 to ¥40.5bn in F12/26.

Daihen: (1) F3/26 results had revenue at ¥237.8bn (+5% YoY; guidance ¥235.0bn) and OP at ¥18.8bn (+16%; ¥18.5bn). (2) F3/27 plan is for revenue of ¥280.0bn (vs. medium-term plan target of ¥250.0bn) and OP ¥25.0bn (¥25.0bn), OP margin 8.9% (10%): Semiconductor and power equipment contributions should drive profit, while Europe and recently acquired domestic subsidiaries will weigh on margins. (3) Power equipment looks strong, with margin improvement a key focus; improving profitability at subsidiaries remains a challenge..

Japan Material: (1) F3/26 results showed revenue of ¥58.0bn (+10% YoY; guidance ¥57.0bn) and OP ¥14.6bn (+31%; ¥13.0bn). (2) F3/27 guidance is for revenue of ¥61.0bn (+5% YoY) and OP ¥15.5bn (+6%): “Initial” segments are expected to see revenue decline, while “operations” are expected to see growth. Inflation, including higher labor costs, are to be passed through to service pricing to maintain margins.
